description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by the #1808 review probe; PRE-EXISTING on main 4c6565e5.  LOW priority: both are documented perl gotchas that working programs AVOID (perlop "The empty pattern //", perlfunc split "when assigning to a list, if LIMIT is omitted ... one larger than the number of variables"), filed so they are not re-derived.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3): ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p-regex-quirks.pl (+ .perl.out / .main-4c6565e5.out)
  my $a = "xaby"; $a =~ /ab/;                       # a successful match
  (my $e1 = "abc-ab") =~ s//-/g;                    # perl "-c--" (pattern = /ab/) ; PCL "-a-b-c---a-b-" (a true empty pattern)
  my $p = ""; "zzabzz" =~ /$p/ ? "[$&]" : "no"      # perl [ab] ; PCL []
  split //, "abc"                                   # a|b|c in both -- split is EXEMPT from the rule
  my $n = () = split /,/, "a,b,c";                  # perl 1 ; PCL 3   (LIMIT 1 = the whole string as one field)
  my ($x,$y) = split /,/, "a,b,c,d";                # a b in both (the implicit limit 3 is invisible here)

IF TAKEN: (1) the empty-pattern rule is a RUN-time fact for the interpolated spelling (the pattern text is empty after interpolation) and a COMPILE-time fact for the literal; the runtime already keeps the last successful match record -- it would have to keep the last successful SCANNER too (one slot, written where the match record is written; #684 says that record is not block-scoped yet, so the same scoping caveat applies).  `(?:)` stays a true empty pattern.  (2) the split limit is a codegen fact: a list-assignment whose RHS is a bare `split` with no LIMIT gets LIMIT = number of scalar targets + 1, ONLY when the LHS has no array/hash target.  The visible case is the empty-LHS countof idiom; with named scalars it is only an optimisation.

BAR: emission change for (2) -> corpus-diff (expect `() = split` to be rare-to-absent), gen bump, guard rows; `cl/` change for (1) -> full sweep + re/ companion leg.  Do NOT take either inside a perf round.
subject: two perl regex QUIRKS PCL answers "intuitively": an EMPTY pattern (literal `//` or an interpolated empty `/$p/`) means THE LAST SUCCESSFUL PATTERN in m// and s/// (not in split), and `() = split ...` / `my $n = () = split` applies an implicit LIMIT of (targets + 1), so the countof idiom answers 1
